characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: The Technical Feasibility Strategy lever controls the technical risk vs. scope trade-off in demonstrator development. Its primary objective is to demonstrate the feasibility of a platform-neutral and fallback-capable Danish digital identity system, using open standards like FIDO2/WebAuthn and OpenID Connect on privacy-respecting platforms. Key success metrics include the successful completion of demonstrators that showcase secure, standards-based, fallback-capable access models without exclusive reliance on Apple or Google as trust anchors.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with Policy Advocacy Strategy (lever 80b177), as demonstrating technical feasibility amplifies the credibility of policy proposals and advocacy efforts. Additionally, it synergizes with EU Standards Engagement Strategy (lever 2e9016) by providing concrete evidence to support the adoption of platform-neutral standards at both national and European levels.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever conflicts with Procurement Influence Strategy (lever f1c0d8), as focusing solely on technical demonstrator development might lead to overlooking procurement-specific requirements, such as cost implications or vendor responsiveness. Furthermore, it may create tension with Coalition Building Strategy (lever 1731ad) if the focus on technical feasibility leads to neglecting coalition-building efforts or underestimating the importance of diverse stakeholder support.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: The Policy Advocacy Strategy lever controls the political risk vs. coalition size trade-off in shaping procurement decisions. Its primary objective is to influence AltID requirements by reframing the issue in terms of resilience, continuity of service, procurement neutrality, and supplier concentration risk, while also addressing privacy and democratic accountability concerns. Key success metrics include securing a formal written response from Digitaliseringsstyrelsen or another relevant authority to the project's proposal.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with Technical Feasibility Strategy (lever bd43cd), as demonstrating technical feasibility amplifies the credibility of policy proposals and advocacy efforts. Additionally, it synergizes with Procurement Influence Strategy (lever f1c0d8) by shaping procurement decisions to favor platform-neutral and fallback-capable digital identity systems.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever conflicts with EU Standards Engagement Strategy (lever 2e9016), as focusing solely on national policy advocacy might lead to overlooking the broader European context, including regulatory capture by incumbent vendors. Furthermore, it may create tension with Coalition Building Strategy (lever 1731ad) if the focus on policy advocacy leads to neglecting coalition-building efforts or underestimating the importance of diverse stakeholder support.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: The Coalition Building Strategy lever controls the speed vs. breadth of support trade-off in amplifying advocacy efforts. Its primary objective is to build a strong, diverse coalition that includes civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, academic researchers, and security experts, to foster internal debate and increase political pressure for platform neutrality. Key success metrics include stakeholder engagement increased and a stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with Policy Advocacy Strategy (lever 80b177), as building a diverse coalition amplifies the effectiveness of policy advocacy efforts. Additionally, it synergizes with Technical Feasibility Strategy (lever bd43cd) by providing concrete evidence to support the adoption of platform-neutral standards.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever conflicts with Procurement Influence Strategy (lever f1c0d8), as focusing solely on coalition-building might lead to overlooking procurement-specific requirements, such as cost implications or vendor responsiveness. Furthermore, it may create tension with EU Standards Engagement Strategy (lever 2e9016) if the focus on national coalition-building leads to neglecting broader European context and regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: The Procurement Influence Strategy lever controls the specificity vs. implementability trade-off in shaping procurement decisions. Its primary objective is to influence AltID procurement documents to include platform-neutral language, certified fallback authentication paths, and supplier concentration risk considerations. Key success metrics include securing a formal written response from Digitaliseringsstyrelsen or another relevant authority to the project's proposal.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with Policy Advocacy Strategy (lever 80b177), as shaping procurement decisions amplifies the effectiveness of policy advocacy efforts. Additionally, it synergizes with Technical Feasibility Strategy (lever bd43cd) by providing concrete evidence to support the adoption of platform-neutral standards.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever conflicts with Coalition Building Strategy (lever 1731ad), as focusing solely on procurement influence might lead to overlooking coalition-building efforts or underestimating the importance of diverse stakeholder support. Furthermore, it may create tension with EU Standards Engagement Strategy (lever 2e9016) if the focus on national procurement influence leads to neglecting broader European context and regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: The EU Standards Engagement Strategy lever controls the resource allocation vs. scope of influence trade-off in shaping European digital identity standards. Its primary objective is to engage with relevant EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards. Key success metrics include input provided to relevant EU bodies and increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with Technical Feasibility Strategy (lever bd43cd), as providing concrete evidence amplifies the credibility of policy proposals and advocacy efforts at both national and European levels. Additionally, it synergizes with Policy Advocacy Strategy (lever 80b177) by shaping procurement decisions to favor platform-neutral and fallback-capable digital identity systems.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever conflicts with Procurement Influence Strategy (lever f1c0d8), as focusing solely on EU standards engagement might lead to overlooking national procurement-specific requirements, such as cost implications or vendor responsiveness. Furthermore, it may create tension with Coalition Building Strategy (lever 1731ad) if the focus on European context leads to neglecting coalition-building efforts or underestimating the importance of diverse stakeholder support.
